newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROBSON AND TOSHACK DESPERATE FOR CUP SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON AND TOSHACK DESPERATE FOR CUP SUCCESS.

text.p: Two British coaches may sink or swim this week as they try to redeem themselves in vital Spanish Cup fourth round, second leg matches.
Bobby Robson's Barcelona defend a 3-2 lead at Real Madrid on Thursday, while John Toshack's Deportivo Coruna travel to Espanyol on Wednesday after scraping a 2-2 draw in the first leg.
Robson is under fire after his side threw away a 2-0 lead at home for the second time in a month in Sunday's 2-2 draw with Oviedo.

"Unforgivable," read the front page headline in Barcelona sports daily 'El Mundo Deportivo' after the club conceded two goals in the last 15 minutes. Two weeks ago they lost 3-2 at home to unrated Hercules after leading 2-0.
In the past, victories over Real -- especially in the cup -- have helped Barcelona coaches ride through difficult periods.
The most recent example involved Johan Cruyff, Robson's predecessor at the Camp Nou.
Cruyff had an unsteady start, but after the 1990 cup final win over Real, then managed by Toshack, went on to lead the club to successive league titles.
Welshman Toshack badly needs a result to calm unrest at 1995 cup winners Deportivo, who have gone six matches without a win.
There are also off-field problems, with club president Augusto Lendoiro summoned to face FIFA officials on Wednesday in the latest development in the row over the club's stadium closure.
The Spanish federation ordered a one-match closure following a coin-throwing incident but Deportivo went to the Spanish courts and had that decision overturned.
FIFA is strongly opposed to clubs using domestic courts to by-pass their associations and has ordered Deportivo to withraw their action.

In other games, cup holders Atletico look clear favourites to hang on to a 2-0 advantage from the first leg at Compostela. Real Betis and Valencia are likely quarter-finalists after bringing home the same result from away fixtures at Tenerife and Las Palmas respectively.

The most finely balanced ties are those between cup specialists Athletic Bilbao and Racing Santander, the latter winning their home first leg 1-0, and Extremadura and Rayo Vallecano, who shared the honours 2-2 last week.
Second division Lleida visit Celta Vigo deadlocked at 1-1.
